newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico EPR rebels say military offensive suspended.
newsitem.headline: Mexico EPR rebels say military offensive suspended.

text.p: Marxist rebels in a poor southwestern Mexican state said they had ordered their fighters not to launch fresh attacks after two bloody clashes with the army last week.
But the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrillas in Guerrero state did not call a ceasefire and also refused to lay down arms ahead of crucial July 6 congressional elections.
Catholic church leaders and Guerrero election organisers had asked the EPR over the weekend to declare a ceasefire so as not to upset next month's vote.

The group responded with a statement released on Sunday night in the Pacific tourist resort of Acapulco. It said EPR units had "withdrawn to their positions to avoid clashes and have received orders not to carry out offensive military actions so as not to interfere in the upcoming electoral process."
But the declaration, signed by "Commander Antonio," also rejected calls for the rebels to surrender their arms, saying they were needed for self-defence.
"When arms are used for self-defence, surrendering them means opting to die," it said. "Surrendering arms is resigning oneself to carry on being mocked."

The EPR, which first appeared in Guerrero in June 1996 calling for a popular revolt to overthrow President Ernesto Zedillo's government, ended months of calm with last week's clashes. More than nine people died in the gunbattles and at least a dozen others were wounded.
EPR rebels had declared truces before local elections in the states of Guerrero and Mexico but Antonio's latest statement made no mention of a ceasefire.
An EPR statement issued in the southern state of Oaxaca over the weekend said the rebel army's units had all been placed on "general alert" after the battles.
Mexicans elect a new lower house of Congress on July 6, as well as renewing a quarter of the Senate, choosing six state governors and choosing the first elected mayor of Mexico City.
The government has repeatedly rejected calls from the left to open talks with the EPR, saying they are a "terrorist" organisation and promising to use the full force of the law against them.
